The value of the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above  is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(4,5)$ and passes through the point $(6,3).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(4,5)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-4)^{2}=4p(y-5).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(6,3),$ we substitute $x=6$ and $y=3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(6-4)^{2} & =4p(3-5) \\ 4 & =4p(-2) \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =-2(y-5).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-4)^{2} & =-2(y-5) \\ 16 & =-2(y-5) \\ -8 & =y-5 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $-3.$
